newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France pilots postpone strike.
newsitem.headline: Air France pilots postpone strike.

text.p: Air France pilots, drawing back from a showdown which may have forced the resignation of airline chairman Christian Blanc, voted to delay a four-day strike that had been scheduled to start on Sunday.
"Seventy percent of the pilots at the general assembly voted for a delay in the strike," an Air France spokeswoman said after unions met on Friday to review a strike call.

Blanc had threatened to resign if the stoppage went ahead. He had estimated the cost of the strike at one billion francs, which would have dashed his hopes of piloting Air France to financial breakeven this year and an early privatisation.
Pilot unions had called the strike from March 23 to 26, to protest against Blanc's plan to hire 450 younger pilots on lower pay scales.

Blanc wants to cut the flight crew wage bill by 15 percent, to bring it into line with its European and U.S. rivals as part of a three-year plan to boost competitiveness. The company is under pressure to reduce costs, with the European air travel market opening up to full competition next month.
Air France had proposed to hire new pilots at a starting annual gross salary of 220,000 francs, compared to the start-up pay of 330,000 that current pilots received when they began their careers.
